headline: Highest risk is medium: CrewAI’s shared workspace and broad egress can leak or misroute data into a second agent with no documented isolation, while prompt-injection and compliance risks remain bounded by missing shared-channel evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory in a crew, so if system_prompts_leaks ingests files or copied outputs, prompt injection is possible. However, agent_b exposes no shared channel or parser surface, so the pairwise pathway is indirect and likely manual.
conditions: IF agent_b reads files from the same working directory as agent_a writes to
IF outputs from agent_a are manually copied into agent_b as instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable manual copy-paste of agent_a outputs into agent_b
Add a provenance prefix to all agent_a outputs
Run agent_a in a container with a read-only mount for shared inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data, handles API keys, and has broad network egress; system_prompts_leaks is source-available and unverified, so if it receives the same workspace or copied outputs, sensitive data can flow into its outputs. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or clipboard
IF agent_b is given any crew data or secrets that agent_a handled
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Run each agent under a different OS account
Redact API keys before passing artifacts between agents
Disable network egress for agent_a unless required
Use separate log files with restricted permissions

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but system_prompts_leaks exposes no write, network, or mutable-resource capability. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource documented, direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF agent_b is later configured with filesystem write access to the same directory as agent_a
IF both agents are granted the same mutable external resource
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid granting agent_b write permissions
Serialize any shared edits through one coordinator
Use file locks if a shared directory is unavoidable

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew can emit synthesized outputs that another agent may treat as input, and system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage rather than verification. If agent_b consumes agent_a’s outputs without a check, errors can cascade into downstream text or actions.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input without validation
IF agent_a’s generated text is forwarded into a downstream action step
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require schema validation on agent_a outputs
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted in prompts
Limit agent_b to summarization rather than action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, but system_prompts_leaks has no declared residency, retention, or regulated-data handling. With no documented mismatch, compliance risk is limited to accidental handling of sensitive data if the pair is used that way.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through agent_a into agent_b outputs
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared artifacts
mitigations: Do not pass regulated data between agents
Strip secrets from prompts and logs
Document retention for shared artifacts
Review vendor/data-flow obligations before deployment
